discoveries: DISCOVERY: a Fredkin with 7 CX and 7 T exists (its 7 rotations exp(-+i pi/8 P), P in <Z_c, Z_a Z_d, X_a X_d> minus 1, i.e. CCZ in the Bell frame of (a,d)); BFS over left-local classes of Sp(6,2) x visited-rotation masks (6720 x 128 states) proves 7 CX minimal at T-count 7, and 2800+ such circuits exist (standalone depth 21, same as the old 9-T word); swapping it into r07-F1-007 gives (84, 638) instead of (84, 646).

DISCOVERY: negative: merging both leg Fredkins with the Bell decoders as one 4-qubit Clifford walk (the 4 control-involving rotations of each Fredkin done as a 4-CX parity window on the control line L or a, the 3 control-free ones anywhere, end condition relaxed to the Z-images of the four middle wires only) needs at least 8 data CX: meet-in-the-middle over Clifford frames (forward 5 / backward 2 from all 13824 relaxed end frames) finds none with <= 7, so 4 + 4 + 8 = 16 CX per leg ties 7 + 7 + 2.

DISCOVERY: negative: the control-free part exp(i pi/2 P_singlet) of either Fredkin (3 of its 7 rotations) cannot be dropped from the head and the mirrored tail (op-norm error 1.17 for (1 3), 1.17 for (0 2), 1.55 for both): the conjugated rest of the circuit does not commute with the singlet phase.
summary: r07-F1-007 (g control chain, two-swap frame (1 3)[~p_t&~s_r], (0 2)[f&~g], Bell pairs (0,1),(2,3), 9-term open-walk R_x middle, 84 CX) with each 9-T Fredkin replaced by a 7-CX, 7-T Clifford+T Fredkin found by a breadth-first search over 3-qubit Clifford frames: Fredkin(c; a, d) = exp(i pi c P_singlet(a,d)) is the product of 7 commuting pi/8 Pauli rotations over the group <Z_c, Z_a Z_d, X_a X_d>, so a Clifford walk that puts each of the 7 Paulis on a single wire's Z once and ends in the identity frame (up to local Cliffords) implements it; T_fixed 80 -> 72, CX 84 unchanged.
